# David G. Smith - Technical Architect, Author & Strategic Advisor

> David G. Smith is a data scientist, cloud solutions architect, and author based in Washington, DC, specializing in federal technology modernization, geospatial intelligence, noise reduction, and critical thinking frameworks.

David G. Smith works at the intersection of enterprise data architecture and decision science. He has led major modernization initiatives, including the USGS Water Quality Portal migration into the EPA Data Management and Analytics Platform (DMAP) and the cloud-native modernization of EPA Envirofacts. He is the author of the 468-page manual *Critical Thinking: A Practical Guide to Seeing Through Bias, Noise and Manipulation* (August 2026).

## Core Publications

- [Critical Thinking: A Practical Guide to Seeing Through Bias, Noise and Manipulation](https://davidgsmith.net/critical-thinking.html): Complete overview of the 468-page cognitive manual, featuring the AI Crux Test, 102 mapped heuristics, and 17 hands-on drills.
- [Books Catalog](https://davidgsmith.net/books.html): Author index of published works and forthcoming series, including *AI for Small Business*.
- [Thoughts & Perspectives](https://davidgsmith.net/thoughts.html): Technical writings, architectural essays, and notes on cloud data mesh, AI evaluation, and decision-making.

## Key Concepts & Intellectual Contributions

- **The AI Crux Test (Chapter 11):** A 3-step verification protocol designed to counteract LLM hallucinations, automated confirmation loops, and chatbot sycophancy (flattery produced by RLHF alignment).
- **The Four Defense Arcs:** Part I (The Flawed Machine: neural heuristics & Somatic Marker Hypothesis), Part II (Mechanics of Thinking: formal/informal logic & statistical risk), Part III (Information in the Wild: lateral reading, citation laundering & propaganda), Part IV (Advanced Toolkit: second-order consequences, Bayesian updating, premortems & red team stress-testing).
- **102 Mapped Heuristics:** Includes actionable models for Simpson's Paradox, Base Rate Neglect, Chesterton's Fence, the Cobra Problem, Gish Gallop, Motte-and-Bailey defenses, and Ideological Turing Tests.
